**A Dynamic Island for your Android punch-hole camera — running over every app on the phone.**

Not a mock-up and not a wallpaper. Dynamic Camera Punch is a system overlay that turns the camera cutout into a live pill: at rest it is a circle around the hole, indistinguishable from the cutout itself. Something happens, it grows out of the hole to show you; the moment passes, it shrinks back and disappears.

| File | Install this? | Size |
|---|---|---|
| **`dcp-v2.7.0-release.apk`** | **Yes** | 180,643 bytes |
| `dcp-v2.7.0-debug.apk` | Only if you are attaching a debugger | 256,410 bytes |

```
sha256  release  b39630eaff1a294c39a53bbafaacaf44b3b045e5c42e137776f5f0734581fd56
sha256  debug    8e74b3b1bbc04ecb40ad21f116431ee49030b3898253544de564304d76018c69
```

Both APKs are signed with APK Signature Scheme v2 and verify with `apksigner verify` across API 24 to 34. The debug build installs alongside the release one as `com.dcp.punch.debug`, labelled **DCP (debug)**.

> If a download will not install, check its size first. A phone browser that lands on a GitHub *page* rather than the file saves an HTML error page under the `.apk` name, and the installer then reports the APK as corrupt. A file of a few KB is a web page, not an app.

## What it shows

| Source | On the island | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Messages** | The conversation and what was actually said — "Family GC" over "Mum · Did you get the toolbox?" — with the sender's avatar. Tap to open the thread. | Notification access |
| **Media** | The track that is playing, with working play/pause and skip | Notification access |
| **Calls** | The incoming caller, read from the dialer's own notification | Notification access |
| **Timers & alarms** | Live countdown from the clock app | Notification access |
| **Navigation** | Turn-by-turn from the maps app | Notification access |
| **Downloads** | Progress from anything reporting it | Notification access |
| **Charging** | Bolt and battery level the moment you plug in | *nothing* |
| **Battery low** | Level and warning | *nothing* |
| **Ringer** | Silent / vibrate / ring changes | *nothing* |
| **Headphones** | Connect and disconnect | *nothing* |

Grant nothing beyond the overlay permission and the last four still work.

## New in 2.7.0 — the control panel

The island itself is unchanged. This release rebuilds the app you configure it from.

### A floating tab bar

Three icons in a rounded pill above the content, rather than a full-width bar fixed to the bottom edge. The active tab rides in a coloured circle that slides between them and stretches slightly as it travels, so it carries a sense of weight instead of jumping. Lists scroll underneath the pill rather than being cut off by it.

### Categories instead of one long scroll

The first screen is short: a header, the master switch, setup, and four categories — **System events**, **Live cards**, **Gestures**, **Notifications**. Each shows a strip of the icons it contains and opens its own screen, sliding in from the right with a back arrow and a **Guide** button explaining what the category is for.

The top level says what the island can do. Only the screen below it asks you to make individual choices.

### Switches that carry a mark

Every toggle shows a tick when it is on and a cross when it is off, on a thumb that slides between them. Colour alone is the one channel a colour-blind user does not have and a bright screen washes out; a mark survives both. The whole row is the target, not just the switch.

### Icons on every row

Around forty of them, drawn directly on a Canvas rather than loaded as image files — one class instead of forty XML drawables, no resource lookups, and nothing held in memory for rows scrolled off screen. Badges are tinted by category, never by state: blue for system events, pink for anything read from notifications.

### A new palette

The previous one was near-black with a hard blue accent, which made card edges disappear into the background and every accent shout. Cards now sit a clear step above the background so a list reads as a list, and the accent is a quieter periwinkle that can head every section without dominating the page.

### Consistent across all three tabs

Island and Settings were rebuilt in the same vocabulary as Cards — section header, card, toggle row, value row, navigation row, note — so the app reads as one thing rather than three. Notification mode, auto-hide delay and "show only on the island" moved into the Notifications screen.

### Fixed

The content allow-list stores *empty means everything*, so the first switch turned off could not simply be removed — the list would still be empty, still mean everything, and the switch would spring back on. Turning one off while the list is empty now writes every other kind in first, then removes the one that was touched.

## How it works

**A system overlay, not a launcher widget.** The island is a `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` window owned by a foreground service, so it draws above every app on the device — home screen, launcher, games, anything.

**Drawn on a Canvas, not built from widgets.** An overlay window has to be exactly the size of its touchable content, because every pixel it covers is a pixel the app underneath stops receiving touches on. The island changes size constantly, so its window is re-measured on every animation frame. That is cheap for a custom `View` and ruinous for anything heavier. One interpolator — `cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)` — carries the whole morph between states.

**The camera never moves.** The overlay window is centre-anchored and the lens is drawn at a fixed offset inside the island, so no state change can slide the hole off the physical sensor.

**Content comes from a `NotificationListenerService` and `MediaSessionManager`.** Message text is parsed from the notification's own `MessagingStyle` data, which is why the island can show what was actually said rather than just an app name. Charging, battery, ringer and headphone events are ordinary system broadcasts and need no permission at all.

**No libraries.** No AndroidX, no Kotlin runtime, no third-party code of any kind — the framework `View` and `Canvas` only. That is why a system-wide overlay, a three-tab control panel, an offline support page and a full browser demonstration fit in 181 KB.

### Memory

The working set is **30–45 MB** and stays there. Two mechanisms, which combine:

- **Automatic management** (on by default) — releases cached avatars and album art for anything not currently on the pill, and acts on every system memory warning rather than only the critical one.
- **A ceiling** you set on the gauge. Crossing 80% of it triggers the same trim early. It is a limit, not a target: the app will not grow to fill it. The range runs from 45 MB up to the RAM Android reports for the device, less 1.5 GB reserved for the system.

### Permissions

Six, each one used by code in the app:

| Permission | Why |
|---|---|
| `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` | Draw the island over other apps. This *is* the product. |
| `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `…_SPECIAL_USE` | The island must survive you leaving the app. |
| `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` | The ongoing notice Android requires for a service that runs indefinitely. It is also how you turn the theme off. |
| `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` | Optional "start on boot", off by default. |
| `BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE` | Read notifications and media sessions. Granted in Settings, revocable at any time. |
| `&lt;queries&gt;` (not a permission) | Lets the app picker list apps that have a launcher icon. |

**Not requested:** `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, `READ_PHONE_STATE`, and `INTERNET` — the app has never made a network request and cannot. Notifications are read only; nothing is stored or sent anywhere.

---

## Setup

1. **Display over other apps** — required. This is what lets the island draw on top of everything, and it is granted in Settings rather than by a dialog.
2. **Notification access** — optional but recommended. This is what makes the content real rather than just charging and ringer events.
3. **Show notifications** — Android requires an ongoing notification for a service that runs indefinitely.

Minimum Android 7.0 (API 24) · targetSdk 34 · about 181 KB on disk.

---

## Known limitations

- Some manufacturer skins — notably Xiaomi/MIUI and some Huawei builds — add their own extra "show on top" toggle and aggressively kill background services. If the island vanishes after a while, that is the vendor's battery manager and the app has to be exempted there.
- **This build has not been run on physical hardware.** It compiles clean, passes Android Lint with zero errors, and its structure and signature verify, but that is not the same as a device test — and 2.7.0 rewrote most of the interface. Please open an issue with a screenshot if something looks wrong.
- The bundled support page ships without a QR image. Drop a `donate-qr.png` into `android/app/src/main/assets/support/` and rebuild to add one.
